<a data-pjax="true" title="Add separate nginx rate limit zone for service traffic and fix local timezone (#10156)

* Add separate nginx rate limit zone for service traffic

All LMS traffic reaches h with the same Authorization header, so under
the per-user zone it collapses into a single 4r/s bucket. Give requests
that carry a Hypothesis-Application header their own zone (50r/s,
burst 100) instead, keyed on the Authorization header, while excluding
them from the general per-user zone.

nginx skips rate-limit accounting when a zone's key is empty: app
requests get an empty key in user_limit and a real key in svc_limit,
and everyone else is untouched.

Only user_limit switches to the header-aware key. The badge and
annotation-creation zones keep the original per-user key: nginx only
applies the limit_req directives of the most-specific matched location,
and those locations carry no svc_limit directive, so an empty key there
would mean no limit at all — and the header is client-settable.

Note: the header is client-settable, so a third-party API client could
opt into the higher bucket — this is a limit raise, not a bypass, which
is why app traffic is still capped rather than fully exempted.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Close rate-limit bypass for no-auth requests with the app header

* fix(date): show user local date instead of utc

the Docker container as this is quicker to do. We can then upgrade
everything to a newer Python at our leisure." class="Link--secondary" href="/hypothesis/h/commit/99eb014bbdcfca1bcedf4ffd1b6ecef0ccde1326">Downgrade the dev env and CI to Python 3.11</a>

<div class="react-directory-commit-message">
<a data-pjax="true" title="Flatten the directory structure for new frontend apps

The new frontend UI was organized into two bundles, login-forms and group-forms,
each of which had subdirectories for components, hooks and utilities. This
structure is awkward for re-arranging bundles or sharing components between
bundles. For example we have started to use the new UI for various account
settings forms. These currently live in the login-forms bundle, but should
really go in a separate bundle.

To make re-arranging and sharing code between bundles easier, flatten the
directory structure and remove the login-forms and group-forms directories:

 - Merge the `{login-forms, group-forms}/routes.ts` modules
 - Merge the `{login-forms, group-forms}/config.ts` modules
 - Move `login-forms/index.tsx` entry point to `login-forms.tsx`
 - Move `group-forms/index.tsx` entry point to `group-forms.tsx`
 - Merge `{login-forms, group-forms}/components` into a new `components`
   directory. This required renaming the `AppRoot` components to avoid a
   conflict.
 - Move `group-forms/{hooks, utils}` to parent directory

The generated bundles are the same as before, but it would now be easier for
example to create a new profile-forms bundle." class="Link--secondary" href="/hypothesis/h/commit/4e4ee43e0a7f9a560e8ea9f4203ab7680613c45b">Flatten the directory structure for new frontend apps</a>

<p dir="auto">First you'll need to install:</p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li>
<a href="https://git-scm.com/" rel="nofollow">Git</a>
.
On Ubuntu: 
<code>sudo apt install git</code>
, on macOS: 
<code>brew install git</code>
.
</li>
<li>
<a href="https://www.gnu.org/software/make/" rel="nofollow">GNU Make</a>
.
This is probably already installed, run 
<code>make --version</code>
 to check.
</li>
<li>
<a href="https://github.com/pyenv/pyenv">pyenv</a>
.
Follow the instructions in pyenv's README to install it.
The 
<strong>Homebrew</strong>
 method works best on macOS.
The 
<strong>Basic GitHub Checkout</strong>
 method works best on Ubuntu.
You 
<em>don't</em>
 need to set up pyenv's shell integration ("shims"), you can

<a href="https://github.com/pyenv/pyenv#using-pyenv-without-shims">use pyenv without shims</a>
.
</li>
<li>
<a href="https://www.docker.com/products/docker-desktop/" rel="nofollow">Docker Desktop</a>
.
On Ubuntu follow 
<a href="https://docs.docker.com/desktop/install/ubuntu/" rel="nofollow">Install on Ubuntu</a>
.
On macOS follow 
<a href="https://docs.docker.com/desktop/install/mac-install/" rel="nofollow">Install on Mac</a>
.
</li>
<li>
<a href="https://nodejs.org/" rel="nofollow">Node</a>
 and npm.
On Ubuntu: 
<code>sudo snap install --classic node</code>
.
On macOS: 
<code>brew install node</code>
.
</li>
<li>
<a href="https://yarnpkg.com/" rel="nofollow">Yarn</a>
: 
<code>sudo npm install -g yarn</code>
.
</li>
</ul>
<p dir="auto">Then to set up your development environment:</p>
<div class="snippet-clipboard-content notranslate position-relative overflow-auto">
<pre lang="terminal" class="notranslate"><code>git clone https://github.com/hypothesis/h.git
cd h
make services
make devdata
make help
</code>

<p dir="auto">

<a href="https://github.com/dependabot">Dependabot</a>

dependencies up to date by sending automated pull requests to all our repos.
But if you need to upgrade or downgrade a package manually you can do that
locally.
</p>
